Covers are countable (finite covers are padded by empty sets). The diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances, with diameter of the empty set zero and unbounded diameter +∞; an empty member contributes zero. 143: ## Auditor execution protocol
144: 
145: The sections below implement the shared requirements. Reviewer identity,
146: fresh packet replay, negative controls, evidence capture and verdict handling
147: are auditor/controller duties; they are not extra mathematical facts for an
148: NL0 author. Mathematical FAIL findings identify the applicable shared table
149: ID and the exact unsupported implication. If the permission boundary itself
150: is ambiguous, disclose that ambiguity rather than silently raising the bar.
151: 
152: Use [self-containment](self-containment.md) and the
153: [audit template](../templates/audit-a.md). New acceptance requires spec/graph
154: v2 and audit v3. Historical PASS records do not satisfy these requirements.
155: 
156: This audit does not use a successful project Lean build as evidence that the
157: NL proof is correct. Querying pinned mathlib for source signatures is allowed;
158: reusing the target's historical Lean proof/verdict requires explicit disclosure
159: and does not establish an independent NL audit.
160: 
161: ## A0. Freeze and disclose
162: 
163: Read the original problem and independently check `spec.json`: target,
164: quantifiers, all H roots, parameter ranges, definitions, representatives,
165: normalization, endpoint conventions, and one-target scope. No H may originate
166: from the proof writer's desired conclusion. Audit target semantics, not just
167: hash equality. Record reviewer/carrier, shared context, read artifacts, and
168: whether any reference solution was seen. Read the canonical graph, not only
169: its generated Markdown. Bind the receipt to spec/graph hashes.
170: Generate the exhaustive global index with
171: `python3 scripts/nl0.py overview nl0.json --spec spec.json --out global-overview.json`.
172: It preserves every actual H (including unused or late-appended H), full global
173: statements/definitions and dependency edges with canonical pointers and hashes.
174: Read this inventory before claiming a node/condition is absent; a partial line
175: page cannot establish absence. The index supplies no verdict and does not
176: replace inspection of the relevant canonical proof and primary-source content.
177: The clean test adapter uses this same core generator, not a separate inventory
178: or mathematical standard.
179: Original-problem/source fidelity and local proof validity are separate tasks.
180: The original text may be read for target and citation checks; it may not fill
181: missing content during per-R packet-only replay. Record the actual boundary.
182: Check that original conditions really are H nodes, rather than predicates
183: hidden in a globally visible parameter type. A prime/nonzero condition,
184: characteristic constraint, range or equation must not become available to an
185: R with empty inputs through that encoding. Matching the full closed theorem
186: alone does not establish correct per-R H availability.
187: 
188: ## A1. Definitions and notation
189: 
190: For each D record a verdict with a concrete explanation. Check unique meaning,
191: type/domain, global versus local binding, definition dependencies, construction
192: or existence prerequisites, and applicability at every use. A guarded symbol
193: must not supply its own prerequisite. Record arbitrary choices, parameter
194: dependencies, and equivalence to the original definition. No project theorem
195: may hide as a definition, record field, predicate, or typeclass assumption.
196: 
197: Reverse-check every actual mathematical object occurrence against a legitimate
198: declaration. Inspect local introduction position, first use, type/domain,
199: basis and end scope. Input-bound variables are not free locals; witnesses need
200: proved existence. Merely checking registered symbol names misses unregistered
201: ones. Definitions cannot smuggle properties or extra ancestor statements.
202: 
203: ## A2. Sources
204: 
205: For each M read the pinned official file and a successful full Lean signature
206: probe, not merely a `#check` name or a search result. Confirm declaration kind,
207: restatement, all implicit/typeclass assumptions, source hashes and commit,
208: relevant axioms, and suitability of scalar fields/domains. Library definitions
209: are not theorems. These source checks belong to global review; each using R's
210: packet review inspects its actual application mappings and premise discharge.
211: 
212: For each E execute all nine requirements in
213: [external-theorem review](external-theorems.md). Give separate evidence-bound
214: verdicts for document identity, occurrence of the actual result, faithful
215: statement, complete surrounding context, and version/source eligibility.
216: Record every actual application separately in its using R, including repeated
217: uses of E in one R; packet review checks those applications. Global review
218: checks the source identity and statement. Source existence, exact citation and valid application are separate
219: obligations. Substantive transformations require an N proof. Do not infer any
220: of these verdicts from a historical audit or a successful Lean build.
221: 
222: ### Paywalled or inaccessible primary text
223: 
224: If a paywalled paper cannot be downloaded or read in full, first search Google
225: using its title, DOI and authors for a downloadable copy or a full-text viewing
226: resource, including author manuscripts and repositories. If that does not
227: provide the text, search Sci-Hub using the DOI or article URL and attempt to
228: download or view it through the user's browser. The user-provided entry point
229: is https://sci-hub.box/. Follow this order: Google, then Sci-Hub.
230: 
231: A readable full-text version is sufficient; downloading a PDF is not required
232: when the theorem and its governing context can be inspected directly. Apply
233: the normal identity, version, statement and context checks to any obtained
234: copy. Record the version actually inspected, rather than treating a preprint
235: as a verified copy of an inaccessible published edition.
236: 
237: If the necessary text remains inaccessible after both searches, record the E
238: ID, bibliographic identifier, attempted searches/access routes and outcomes,
239: and the citation checks that could not be performed. Skip those blocked
240: citation-correctness checks and continue the remaining NL0/Audit A work. Keep
241: completed checks and their evidence; mark the unperformed checks and the
242: source's overall review UNVERIFIED, explaining the access limitation in the
243: notes. Do not record a skipped check as PASS or infer an incorrect citation
244: merely from lack of access. Any downstream judgments depending on the source
245: must disclose that unresolved source verification.
246: 
247: In the final user-facing report, explicitly list every such E, what remains
248: unchecked, the retrieval attempts and the text needed to complete the review.
249: Do not leave this notification only in a machine-readable log. An access
250: failure alone is not a substantive mathematical gap and does not require

251: halting all other work, but the incomplete audit cannot receive an unqualified
252: DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED verdict. Use the existing UNVERIFIED verdict and
253: `inspect-audit` for complete unresolved records; do not invent evidence or
254: primary-source contents to satisfy a mechanical gate.
255: 
256: ## A3. Structure
257: 
258: Run `nl0.py check`. Confirm that every retained node is on P's dependency
259: closure and every internal/target has one complete producer. Derive reachability
260: by AND closure: accept an R's output only after all its inputs are accepted and
261: the R itself passes mathematical review. Mere existence of a path is inadequate.
262: Only E/M/H are trusted source proposition kinds; a proof with no mathematical
263: inputs must still contain an actual permitted calculation/logical argument.
264: 
265: ## A4. Review every inference
266: 
267: Apply verified-background-1 while retaining every check below. An eligible
268: omitted basic fact receives a positively checked background note and does not
269: fail solely for missing input accounting. Ordinary correct elementary
270: compression needs no exhaustive displayed chain. Substantive missing grounds,
271: conditions, sources or proof still block. The accepted local material includes
272: the version-bound supplement; it cannot be reconstructed silently from memory.
273: 
274: First check three closures from the actual text:
275: 
276: - **statement_closure**: input/output statements include every claimed formula,
277:   condition, binder and semantic convention. No producer proof is needed to
278:   understand them. Source notation and inherited equation numbers are not content.
279: - **object_closure**: actual object occurrences map to legitimate declarations
280:   in scope. Compare text to the inventory, not the inventory to itself. Check
281:   input instantiation, witness existence and parameter dependence.
282: - **dependency_closure**: actual factual uses map to direct inputs, prior
283:   in-scope local proofs or fixed logical/calculation steps. An ancestor not
284:   listed as input is unavailable; prior/source proof bodies supply no extra fact.
285: 
286: Then check the six mathematical obligations below. Every check needs a separate
287: `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}` record with precise packet locations and
288: an explanation. Repeating author notes or generic assurances is not review.
289: 
290: 1. **inputs**: the cited propositions are the actual graph inputs and true
291:    earlier results, original H, or verified sources. They are instantiated
292:    with compatible parameters and definitions.
293: 2. **argument**: every step is justified and sufficient. Explicitly inspect
294:    domain, limits, operator applications, integrability, sign, constants,
295:    uniformity, degeneracies, and selected witnesses where material.
296: 3. **dependency_accounting**: each declared input has an identifiable role;
297:    no additional nontrivial theorem is hidden in “clearly,” an analogy,
298:    a definition, or a convenient abstract interface. Locally derived facts are
299:    permitted only after their derivation. This is accounting for the present
300:    argument, not a claim that its input set is minimal across all proofs.
301:    A named theorem is also an imported fact unless its full required result
302:    is actually proved locally. Explaining why its hypotheses hold is an
303:    application check, not a proof of that theorem. For example, “apply FTC,”
304:    “Fubini applies because the function is integrable,” “compactness gives
305:    uniform continuity,” and “a dominated limit may be integrated” require
306:    declared E/M inputs or complete earlier local proofs of the needed results.
307:    Familiarity, a descriptive theorem name, or inclusion in an author-written
308:    calculation-policy sentence cannot waive this obligation. Ordinary valid textbook compression is allowed for eligible background;
309:    substantive tools and missing arguments still need their actual grounds.
310:    An abstract finite-dimensional, tensor or localization lemma is not
311:    automatically a finite arithmetic identity: inspect its displayed map,
312:    inverse, basis or other derivation, or require the actual declared source.
313: 4. **output**: the derived theorem is exactly the output's full statement,
314:    including quantifier order, assumptions, scope, constants and endpoints.
315: 5. **scope**: temporary assumptions are correctly closed into the implication,
316:    negation, cases, or other allowed rule. Check binder freshness and witness
317:    escape. Introduce/discharge metadata alone is not proof. Do not reclassify
318:    a temporary assumption as an original H.
319: 6. **applicability**: check every E/M obligation using its actual bindings and
320:    input/local proofs, including any proved bridge. For each E application A
321:    record separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews and the N
322:    bridge IDs. “The theorem applies” is not a hypothesis mapping.
323: 
324: Finally complete **packet_replay**, the tenth check. A fresh context reviews
325: the exact packet, Yui rules and logged pinned-mathlib queries for verified
326: background, without original-source proofs, other R
327: bodies, old NL0, author audit notes or prefilled verdicts. Record actual carrier,
328: packet hash, prior exposure, mathematical materials read and execution evidence.
329: Source fidelity is a separate check. Same-context rereading is a diagnostic,
330: not fresh replay. This standard does not authorize new agent/service dispatch;
331: keep an unperformed replay UNVERIFIED. Metadata cannot authenticate a claimed
332: identity or isolation; preserve actual execution evidence and disclose limits.
333: 
334: For an authorized clean packet replay, expose only that frozen packet as a
335: task document, plus the Yui procedure. The clean packet carrier exposes controlled read-only pinned-mathlib
336: queries and source probes for background notes, never arbitrary local files.
337: Source/signature verification is a separate stage with its own disclosed inputs.
338: 
339: Use `audit-template` for scaffolds. Every generated verdict starts UNVERIFIED.
340: Serialization may preserve actually made judgments, but cannot infer PASS from
341: author notes, populated fields, successful hashes or absence of exceptions.
342: Ineligible missing content blocks acceptance. Eligible routine background
343: may be positively checked and recorded, never silently assumed from memory. Return the defect to authoring and review the newly frozen version.
344: 
345: Stop granting acceptance at the first unsupported implication. Other diagnostic
346: checks may continue, but a blocked descendant cannot receive a whole-proof
347: pass. Report exact premises -> conclusion and the affected closure. Repairs
348: require a new graph hash and replacement audit, never a silently stronger H.
349: 
350: An ordinary omission or verifiable local mistake may return to routine NL0
351: completion without interrupting the user for each correction. Review the
352: revised argument before accepting it. If completion stalls, apply
353: [routine completion and substantive proof gaps](nl0-authoring.md#routine-completion-and-substantive-proof-gaps)
354: to assess whether construction must stop; do not turn every omitted detail
355: into a substantive-gap report or silently begin a new proof strategy.
356: 
357: ## A5. Adversarial target checks
358: 
359: Check actual excluded/included endpoints, zero/degenerate objects, a.e. versus
360: everywhere, scalar/representation changes, and constant uniformity. Negative
361: controls must distinguish machine-detectable corruption (unknown IDs, changed
362: evidence) from semantic corruption (wrong argument with unchanged structure).
363: A failed counterexample search or a valid JSON file cannot establish correctness.
364: 
365: ## Acceptance and report
366: 
367: Behavioral controls must include an opaque formula output, a source-only object,
368: an unlisted theorem and an unsupported witness. A real reviewer receives neutral
369: packets without labels, old reviews or expected answers; the owner's answer key
370: stays outside its input directory. Require located findings, not just verdicts.
371: Manually assigning FAIL only tests receipt handling, not model detection. If no
372: reviewer ran, report NOT_RUN. `prepare-review-cases.py --help` prepares a small
373: control set without calling a model or claiming an isolation experiment.
374: 
375: Grant `DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED` only if A0–A5 are actually completed for the exact
376: frozen artifact, every required review is PASS, source evidence is verified,
377: and P closes without extra assumptions. Say “same-context self-audit” when
378: that is the execution mode. `nl0.py --audit` verifies the hash-bound review
379: record's completeness, not the truth of the reviewer statements. Preserve any
380: FAIL/UNVERIFIED report and identify the first gap; do not erase it after repair.
381: For access-limited sources, finish with an explicit pending-citation list and
382: an incomplete/UNVERIFIED audit outcome while reporting the other completed
383: checks. Skipping unavailable citation checks does not waive them for a future
384: whole-proof pass.

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This is the detailed meaning of Audit A's `statement_closure`,
4: `object_closure` and `dependency_closure` requirements. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound verified background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under verified-background-1, local review may additionally verify routine
25: pinned-mathlib facts using logged read-only queries and record them in the
26: receipt. They join this R's effective dependencies, without new H or a graph
27: rewrite. See [background notes](background-notes.md). Mathematical uncertainty
28: still blocks; ordinary correct elementary compression alone does not.
29: 
30: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
31: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
32: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
33: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
34: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
35: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
36: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
37: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
38: 
39: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
40: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
41: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
42: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
43: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
44: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
45: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
46: 
47: ## Object closure
48: 
49: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
50: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
51: 
52: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
53:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
54:    cover mathematical language and the fixed logic/finite calculations only;
55:    they cannot license unnamed analysis theorems.
56: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
57:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
58:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
59: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
60:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
61:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
62:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
63: 
64: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
65: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
66: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
67: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
68: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
69: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
70: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
71: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
72: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
73: 
74: ## Dependency closure
75: 
76: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
77: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
78: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible omitted basic library uses are
79: recorded as verified audit notes in the effective dependency ledger. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
80: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
81: 
82: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
83: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
84: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
85: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
86: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
87: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
88: 
89: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the primitive vocabulary
90: (`scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
91: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
92: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
93: theorem. Such facts need a declared input or an actual local derivation.
94: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
95: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
96: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
97: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
98: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
99: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
100: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
101: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
102: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
103: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
104: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
105: 
106: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
107: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
108: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
109: 
110: ## Operational acceptance
111: 
112: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
113:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
114: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
115:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
116:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
117:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
118: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
119:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
120: 4. Perform a fresh local replay with disclosed controlled background lookup. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
121:    and that packet plus logged pinned-mathlib queries, without original proof,
122:    other R bodies, author review
123:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
124:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
125:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
126:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
127:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
128:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
129:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
130:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
131:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
132: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
133:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
134:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
135:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
136:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
137:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
138: 
139: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
140: and receipts. Its reference-pattern checks are conservative diagnostics, not a
141: parser for all mathematical language. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
142: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
143: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
144: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

1: # External-theorem review: required Audit A standard
2: 
3: Apply this standard to every retained E and every actual use of E in an R.
4: An E keeps the full source theorem; a derived specialization or substantive
5: translation is an internal N. Use the data contract's audit version 2. These
6: are reviewer obligations: a filled record or matching hash cannot establish
7: that a publication or a mathematical assertion is genuine.
8: 
9: ## 1. Document identity
10: 
11: Obtain and read the actual primary document. Match author, title, source kind,
12: publication/release information and exact edition/version to its provenance.
13: Record a traceable original source, retrieval date, local document and hash.
14: A search snippet, model answer, secondary citation, or functioning DOI/URL
15: alone does not establish identity. Books, papers and reliable preprints can
16: qualify; a DOI and journal publication are not universal requirements. Record
17: the source category and grounds for treating it as an admissible source.
18: 
19: For paywalled or inaccessible text, use Audit A's
20: [Google-then-Sci-Hub retrieval procedure](audit-a.md#paywalled-or-inaccessible-primary-text).
21: If access still fails, skip the blocked citation checks with an explicit
22: UNVERIFIED record, continue the remaining work, and notify the user in the
23: final report. This is a deferred check, not a source-verification pass. Do not
24: replace unavailable primary text with model recollection or a search summary.
25: 
26: ## 2. Occurrence of the result
27: 
28: Locate the claimed result in that document and version. Record theorem,
29: lemma, proposition or corollary label and page/section/paragraph/equation as
30: available; unnumbered results require an equally reproducible locator. Retain
31: the relevant primary text or a precise readback record bound to the document.
32: If the cited document merely points elsewhere without actually stating the
33: claimed result, follow and correct the source. An explicitly stated theorem in
34: an authoritative exposition can be cited as such; record its proof attribution
35: without claiming to have audited the referenced proof recursively.
36: Distinguish proved assertions from conjectures, questions, heuristics and
37: numerical observations. Preserve every condition of a conditional result.
38: 
39: ## 3. Statement fidelity
40: 
41: Compare the original full statement with the E statement, explicitly covering
42: objects, domains, scalar fields, spaces, hypotheses, regularity, quantifier
43: order, parameter intervals/endpoints, degeneracies, constant dependencies and
44: the exact conclusion (including a.e./everywhere, topology, uniformity,
45: existence/uniqueness and local/global scope). Record the notation map.
46: Faithful mathematical meaning, not word-for-word copying, is required.
47: Alpha-renaming is allowed. Never turn forall-x-exists-C_x into exists-C-forall-x.
48: 
49: ## 4. Complete context and definitions
50: 
51: Read the surrounding standing assumptions, definitions and conventions that
52: govern the result, including referenced context needed to understand it.
53: Capture any omitted chapter-wide hypotheses and normalization of measures,
54: norms, transforms, signs or scales. Map the source objects to the global D
55: ledger. Do not hide a condition outside the proof graph. A substantive
56: conversion requires an N proof; a renamed symbol is not that proof.
57: 
58: ## 5. Version status and source eligibility
59: 
60: Match every locator and statement to the chosen version. Check available
61: primary version histories, corrections, errata or withdrawal information at
62: the recorded date and scope. Record relevant findings and their effect;
63: explain use of an older version. Absence of a discovered correction is not
64: a guarantee that none exists. Unresolved conflicts remain UNVERIFIED.
65: Never import the target, an unproved project lemma, or a circular dependency
66: as E. Previously proved project modules require an expanded graph or a
67: versioned proof handoff. Do not attribute a combination of sources and a
68: project bridge to a single published theorem. A conjecture-dependent theorem
69: must retain that condition, which must be supplied legitimately at application.
70: 
71: ## 6. Every actual application
72: 
73: Give each actual E application an inference-local A ID. The same E applied
74: twice with different bindings has two A records, even within the same R.
75: For each A inspect the parameter/object bindings, prove every source
76: hypothesis from declared inputs or displayed local derivations, check types,
77: definitions and parameter ranges, identify substantive bridge N nodes, and
78: verify the resulting conclusion supports R's output. Record the evidence for
79: each individual hypothesis. “The theorem applies” is not a mapping.
80: Do not add an unproved hypothesis to close an application. An E passed at its
81: source does not automatically pass at any application site.
82: 
83: ## 7. Ownership of derived work
84: 
85: Put substantive specialization, scaling, change of normalization/domain/space/
86: norm/representation, combinations of sources, and prerequisite lemmas in N.
87: Each N lists its actual E/M/H/earlier-N inputs and its argument. Do not enlarge
88: the quoted theorem. Explicit elementary calculations and logical instantiation
89: may remain inside R; justify them rather than imposing needless graph nodes.
90: 
91: ## 8. Separate decisions and reproducible evidence
92: 
93: For each E write five separate review records: `literature_identity`,
94: `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`, `context_completeness`, and
95: `version_and_eligibility`. Each contains verdict, concrete notes and hashed
96: evidence. The first three must never be merged into one blanket PASS.
97: For each R/A write separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews,
98: the source ID and the proved bridge IDs. Record actual reviewer, carrier,
99: shared context and reference material read. Self-audit is not independent.
100: 
101: Use PASS only after the check was performed with adequate evidence; FAIL for
102: an established mismatch/omission/invalid application; UNVERIFIED when necessary
103: evidence is missing. Inaccessible text does not establish nonexistence. An
104: established absence of the claimed result in the cited source is a FAIL.
105: Retain failed records and the exact reason, source location and affected nodes.
106: 
107: ## 9. Acceptance, invalidation and trust boundary
108: 
109: Every retained E check and every application must PASS before the graph can
110: receive DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED. A load-bearing FAIL/UNVERIFIED blocks descendants
111: and whole-proof acceptance; diagnostic review may continue. Never replace a
112: missing verification with a historical audit or a Lean build. Changes to the
113: source/version, statement, definitions, bindings or condition proofs invalidate
114: affected reviews; bind the replacement whole receipt to new canonical hashes.
115: 
116: An inaccessible source suspends its citation verification, not the rest of
117: the workflow: continue available checks and explicitly conditional reasoning,
118: then report the unfinished citation checks and the UNVERIFIED overall audit
119: outcome. Descendants cannot receive an unconditional pass based on that
120: source, and source inaccessibility alone is not a finding of mathematical error.

122: List all external dependencies in the final verdict. This audit is relative
123: to those identified theorems; it does not independently reprove their published

125: coverage and byte consistency, not authenticity or mathematical correctness.

16: ## Authority and semantics
17: 
18: The isolated authoring carrier offers `check_draft` and `submit_draft`, taking
19: an `artifact` JSON object directly. Prefer these to the compatible older
20: `artifact_json` string wrappers: an additional string-encoding layer is not
21: part of the mathematical format. Both routes execute identical checks.
22: 
23: `spec.json` freezes the original full theorem, the conclusion under its declared
24: parameters/hypotheses, the exact H list, global definition pairs, logic policy,
25: source-input hashes, and Lean/mathlib pins. A human must confirm that this
26: specification matches the original problem; string equality cannot establish
27: semantic fidelity. `nl0.json` references this spec by its SHA256 and duplicates
28: none of its definitions or H statements. One separate spec is required per
29: target. Multiple-target decomposition is outside version 2.
30: 
31: Read a derived proposition as a theorem under the original parameters and the
32: H nodes actually used on its derivation path. All additional free variables are
33: locally quantified in its statement; there are no ambient undeclared claims.
34: An unused original H is allowed and reported; do not silently strengthen or
35: weaken the frozen theorem. E/M results retain their general signatures; apply
36: them through explicit bindings and hypothesis checks in the inference.
37: 
38: Graph vertices are propositions and inferences. Edges are generated only as
39: `input proposition -> inference -> output proposition`. An inference requires
40: all inputs. List order is presentation only: a dependency may occur later in
41: the JSON array, provided the graph admits a topological order. Actual circular
42: dependencies, unknown IDs, and disconnected retained branches fail.
43: 
44: The isolated authoring carrier also reports a hash-bound machine checkpoint of
45: its latest own draft and actual structural result. After a context reset, resume
46: that candidate with `read_draft`/`base_candidate`; do not claim no draft exists or
47: restart the frozen input accidentally. The checkpoint grants no Audit A verdict.

49: ## Specification fields
50: 
51: Use [the authoring template](../templates/authoring.md) and the complete
52: [model-visible submission example](../templates/submission-example.md). The
53: example explains metadata placeholders and local-witness accounting; it is not
54: a benchmark or proof certification. Required top-level spec fields are:
55: 
56: - `format_version: 2`, `case_id`, `full_target`, `conclusion` (nonempty strings);
57: - `parameters`: records `{symbol, type}`; parameter symbols reserve global names.
58:   Give ambient data types/structures only. Original conditions, ranges and
59:   equations belong in H, not in parameter refinements that would be visible
60:   to every R;
61: - `hypotheses`: records `{id: Hddd, statement, origin}` extracted before authoring;
62: - `definitions`: records `{id: Dddd, symbol, definition, type, depends_on,
63:   requires, binders, objects}`. Each symbol has exactly one global meaning. `depends_on` lists
64:   earlier/resolvable D IDs and is acyclic. `requires` lists proved H/N IDs that
65:   must already be available whenever the definition is used;
66: - `logic`: `{classical: boolean, rules: [names], calculations: [fixed IDs],
67:   primitives: [{symbol, type, meaning}]}`. In the clean author tool, omit
68:   `calculations` and `primitives` to bind the controller's fixed language profile.
69:   Optional calculation IDs are `equality`, `definitions`, `finite_algebra`,
70:   `finite_order`, `finite_sums`. Optional primitive selections may be
71:   `{symbol: ...}`; the controller validates selections and binds the complete
72:   fixed vocabulary with exact type/meaning. A new
73:   Audit A requires the bound metadata. Author-defined permission descriptions
74:   and conflicting primitive meanings are rejected, not silently accepted;
75: - `pins`: `{lean_version, mathlib_commit, mathlib_root}`; the root is a local
76:   locator, the version/commit are scientific identifiers;
77: - `inputs`: evidence records `{path, sha256}` for the original problem/proof.

79: The exact machine identifiers permitted in `logic.rules` and inference `rules`
80: are `direct`, `modus_ponens`, `implication_introduction`, `negation_introduction`,
81: `contradiction_classical`, `case_elimination`, `forall_introduction`,
82: `exists_elimination`, and `natural_induction`. Describe algebra/analysis in the
83: actual proof text; it is not a new trusted logical rule. These identifiers
84: describe proof packaging, not a substitute for establishing the implication.

86: The fixed profile in `scripts/foundations.py` permits displayed finite
87: algebra/order calculations and ordinary logic, not analysis theorems. Standard
88: notation such as integral and derivative grants no identity or regularity.
89: Task-specific functions, spaces, derivatives and indicator abbreviations are
90: parameters, D definitions or scoped locals; they cannot be hidden in primitives.

93: Definitions may be globally visible but guarded. Example: “K is the unique
94: fixed curve from N008” requires N008 before K is used. N008 itself must state
95: existence using the previously defined space/operator, without assuming K.
96: Proof prerequisites must be direct inference inputs in v2;
97: the output being proved cannot discharge its own definition prerequisite.

100: ## Proposition fields
101: 
102: Every proposition has `id`, `kind`, the complete `statement`, `definitions`
103: (D IDs), `binders`, and `objects`:

105: - `binders`: `{symbol, type}` records for statement-bound variables. These do
106:   not introduce free variables in a consuming R. Register actual nested scope
107:   in the statement; alpha-rename to avoid global shadowing.
108: - `objects`: distinct names of mathematical objects actually used in the
109:   statement, from frozen parameters/primitives, referenced D closure or these
110:   binders. A D also has these fields for its defining expression.

112: These are inventories, not a parser-generated list. Audit A must find omitted
113: objects by reading actual prose/formulas. Export all formulas and conditions;

118: | `hypothesis` | Hddd | none | exactly matches frozen H statement |

142: Native type printing (and the legacy `#check @declaration` probe) preserves the complete outer telescope,

157: Every submission starts from the immutable named input, not the previous

237: ## Inference fields
238: 
239: Required fields: `id: Rddd`, `inputs` (unique proposition IDs), `output` (one
240: N/P ID), `definitions` (direct D references), `rules` (permitted logic-rule
241: names), `locals`, `argument`, and `applications`.
242: 
243: - `locals`: `{symbol, type, scope}` records. Scope identifies a binding inside
244:   this inference; names cannot shadow globals. Two bindings in different
245:   scopes/nodes may use the same spelling. Bound variables of source theorems
246:   can be alpha-renamed and instantiated. Audit actual binding/freshness.
247:   In v2 also require `start`, `end` (inclusive S IDs), `kind` (`arbitrary`,
248:   `definition`, or `witness`), `declaration` (full introduction), `from_inputs`,
249:   `from_local` (prior F IDs) and `objects` (already available objects used to
250:   introduce this one). A witness must have an input/local existence basis.

251:   The checker verifies declared availability/order, not the existence claim's
252:   semantics. Source-bound variables need a legitimate local instantiation.
253:   The `scope` label and inclusive start/end must agree with the prose. Keep an
254:   object live through its last actual use. Establish an existence F in an
255:   earlier S, then choose its witness in a subsequent S; using a newly produced
256:   F as the witness basis in the same paragraph is a forward reference.
257: - `argument`: ordered records `{id: Sddd, text, uses, uses_local, objects,
258:   produces, introduces, discharges}`. S IDs are inference-local and unique. `uses`
259:   lists direct graph inputs used at this point. Local facts established earlier
260:   in the prose do not become graph inputs. The union of `uses` must equal
261:   `inputs`. A citation's presence is not semantic evidence that it was used.
262:   `uses_local` lists only earlier F IDs; `objects` lists the actually used
263:   global/active local objects. `produces` holds complete local facts
264:   `{id: Fddd, statement, binders, objects, assumptions}`; assumptions lists remaining
265:   local L IDs on which the fact depends. A local fact cannot be used before
266:   its production or outside its assumption/object scope. A paragraph cannot
267:   cite its newly produced F as a previous premise. Formulas to be reused by a
268:   different R must appear in the exported proposition, not only in `produces`.
269: - `introduces`/`discharges`: lists of inference-local assumption IDs (e.g.
270:   `L1`). Temporary assumptions are never proposition vertices. Every introduced
271:   ID is unique in this inference and must be discharged once, no earlier than
272:   introduction. These lists account for prose; Audit A checks the actual
273:   formula, scope, and chosen rule. A correctly closed implication may retain
274:   the assumption in its antecedent. Deleting the ID cannot justify an output.
275: - `applications`: records covering every directly used E/M input, with
276:   `{input, at: Sddd, bindings, hypothesis_checks}`.
277:   `bindings` is a nonempty string spelling out the actual variable/parameter
278:   substitution; it is not a JSON mapping. `hypothesis_checks` is an ordered
279:   list of nonempty strings, one per declared source obligation. For example,
280:   `"bindings": "Set the source parameter a to the current x."` records a
281:   substitution; it does not prove its conditions.
282:   The S paragraph must list
283:   this input in `uses`; only local facts available before that paragraph may
284:   supply application conditions. E applications additionally require
285:   an inference-local unique `id: Addd`; different actual uses of the same E
286:   need separate IDs and records. M may also use explicit A IDs for repeated
287:   instances; a legacy M without `id` uses its input ID as the unique key.
288:   `hypothesis_checks` has one nonempty
289:   explanation for each corresponding source obligation. A hypothesis needs an
290:   actual argument from inputs/H/local proved facts; filling a string is only
291:   an accounting check. Prove substantive normalization bridges as N nodes.
292: 
293: Input-free R nodes are permitted only for explicitly shown calculations or
294: logical/definitional consequences. They are audited proofs, not a fourth kind
295: of trusted source. Transitive inputs need not be repeated unless used directly.

297: ## Audit record
298: 
299: `audit-a.json` contains `format_version`, `graph_sha256`, `spec_sha256`,
300: `reviewer` (`identity`, `mode`, `independent`, `disclosure`), `target_review`,
301: `definition_reviews`, `source_reviews`, and `inference_reviews`.
302: 
303: Each review contains `verdict: PASS|FAIL|UNVERIFIED`, substantive `notes`, and
304: hashed `evidence`. Inference reviews contain ten separate check review objects:
305: `inputs`, `argument`, `dependency_accounting`, `output`, `scope`, `applicability`,
306: `statement_closure`, `object_closure`, `dependency_closure`, `packet_replay`.
307: Each check has `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}`. `locations` contains
308: JSON pointers resolving inside that R's actual packet, such as
309: `/inputs/0/statement` or `/inference/argument/1/text`. PASS requires at least
310: one actual inspected location; a boolean/enum alone is insufficient.
311: Every D, every E/M source, every R, and the target must be covered exactly once.
312: Spec input hashes and source evidence are read back; malformed/duplicate JSON
313: keys, missing files, changed bytes, failed verdicts, and stale audit hashes fail.
314: 
315: Use audit `format_version: 3` for all new records. Audit v1/v2 are readable
316: only with historical graph v1 and `--legacy`; they cannot satisfy this contract.
317: Each E source review additionally has `citation_checks`, mapping exactly
318: `literature_identity`, `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`,
319: `context_completeness`, `version_and_eligibility` to separate ordinary review
320: objects `{verdict, notes, evidence}`.
321: Each version-3 inference review additionally has `external_applications`,
322: mapping exactly its E application A IDs to records
323: `{input, verdict, notes, evidence, bindings_review, hypothesis_reviews,
324: conclusion_review, bridges}`. `input` must match A's E; each nested review
325: has `{verdict, notes, evidence}`; the ordered `hypothesis_reviews` list matches
326: all source obligations one for one. `bridges` lists N nodes already in R's
327: direct input list. A bridge string is not a proof of that bridge.
328: 
329: Each inference review also has `replay: {packet_sha256, mode, carrier,
330: prior_exposure, read_materials}`. Modes are `unperformed`,
331: `same_context_diagnostic`, and `fresh_packet_only`. A passing replay/overall
332: inference requires the actual fresh carrier, empty prior proof exposure, and
333: `read_materials` equal to `["packet:<hash>"]` for mathematical input. Skill
334: instructions supply the procedure, not additional mathematics. The hash must
335: match the regenerated packet. Keep traces as evidence; metadata cannot
336: authenticate a claimed identity or prove truthful isolation.
337: 
338: `audit-template` creates only UNVERIFIED reviews, empty check locations and an
339: unperformed replay. It refuses to overwrite an existing output. It does not
340: inherit author notes or old verdicts. `inspect-audit` can inspect this pending
341: record; `check --audit` rejects it. Each PASS must come from actual review.
342: 
343: `check --audit` accepts only fully passing records. `inspect-audit --audit`
344: also validates the completeness and evidence of FAIL/UNVERIFIED records and
345: returns their unresolved review paths; success of inspection is not proof
346: acceptance. Overall PASS with a failed child review never passes acceptance.
347: 
348: Mode `same_context_self_audit` requires `independent: false`. If claiming an
349: independent review, disclose its actual carrier and input boundary; this file
350: does not authenticate identity or prove independence.

352: ## Local packet
353: 
354: The v2 packet contains `contract_version`, `case_id`, spec/graph hashes,
355: parameters, fixed logic, pins, expanded definitions, complete input/output
356: ports, the current inference, a warning, and `packet_sha256`. Source ports keep
357: applicability obligations and M signatures; primary-document verification is
358: separate. Producer arguments, original-proof locations, source proof text,
359: non-input H and extra ancestor/guard statements are not supplied. Guards must
360: already be direct inputs. The packet intentionally omits the global full target
361: so that its unstated premises cannot become an ambient local hypothesis.
362: 
363: Its digest is SHA256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON (`sort_keys=True`,
364: `ensure_ascii=False`, `separators=(",", ":")`) excluding `packet_sha256`.
365: It is independent of audit-verdict fields, avoiding a circular receipt hash.
366: Packets are generated views and never a second editable proof authority.
367: 
368: ## Mechanical boundaries
369: 
370: The checker validates declared objects, the frozen contract, graph closure,
371: notation-name metadata, citation parity, local-assumption accounting, guarded
372: definition availability, and hash-bound audit coverage. It verifies source
373: checkout/file hashes, not the truth of a source restatement. The printed
374: signature must be obtained from a successful pinned Lean probe and compared by
375: the auditor; an arbitrary string called `signature` is not verification.
376: 
377: The checker cannot establish that a natural-language formula is well typed,
378: that two spellings have the same mathematical meaning, that a hidden theorem
379: was not used, that a local witness did not escape the prose, or that an argument
380: is valid. Those are explicit Audit A obligations. Neither a JSON PASS nor a
381: fabricated complete audit receipt is a mathematical certificate.
382: Numbered-reference diagnostics reject common opaque references, not every
383: possible paraphrase or hidden import. Behavioral tests must actually ask an
384: auditor to review unseen controls; manually prefilled FAIL records only test
385: receipt rejection and must be reported as such.

388:

393: remains unchanged. A new replay uses `fresh_packet_with_verified_background`
394: and binds `library_evidence` plus its actual material hashes; old strict
395: empty-note records can retain `fresh_packet_only`.

397: `nl0.validate` returns the note supplement/hash and note count. A packet read
398: from an accepted source includes its notes and the original reviewed-packet
399: hash. This enriched view is not claimed to be the original replay input.

402: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
403: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
404: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;

1: # Verified background notes
2: 
3: Audit A's shared acceptance section is the single mathematical authority.
4: `verified-background-1` preserves all ten per-R checks and permits ordinary
5: mathematical compression plus positively checked omitted basic mathlib uses.

7: ## Admission
8: 
9: An eligible step is correct, routine and local, has all material conditions
10: already available, and needs neither a new hypothesis nor a new core argument.
11: Check mathematical content, not length or familiarity alone. Major tools remain
12: explicit inputs. Wrong quantifiers, unjustified witnesses/limits, hidden project
13: lemmas and inaccessible external citations still block. A source guess is not
14: verification; API difficulty alone is not a mathematical error.
15: 
16: For example, continuity of a pointwise sum follows from the input continuity
17: and the codomain's continuous addition. A reviewer can probe `Continuous.add`
18: and record that application instead of demanding an epsilon-delta proof or an
19: author rewrite. Arbitrary codomains do not supply continuous addition by name.
20: Elementary arithmetic need not display every intermediate chain; a useful short
21: completion can remain an elementary note, with no imported theorem.

1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning.
